Sea Scrolls, we learn that it was Pharaoh that gave Abraham Hagar. We are also told that Lot took a wife from the "daughters of Egypt." Question: What is the law of Sarah? The law of Sarah is that she gives her husband another wife. Depending on how you read the Pearl of Great Price, and Genesis, Sarah appears to be at least 50 at this time. But they lived longer in those days. Abraham lived to be 175. Now let's get to the meat of Abraham. Here is a man who is promised a posterity forever, and a land, and he has neither. That is pretty strange. How did it make him look? You go around saying that you have a deal with the only God that exists, that you will have a lot of kids, and lands, and you have neither. He is surrounded by kings with many sons and daughters, and lands. What is going on here. How many times does the Lord tell him and reconfirm the covenant with him. He reconfirms it numerous times, as Abraham gets older and older. His actual election apparently does not occur until the sacrifice of Isaac. At that point he gets a new name; until then, the Lord has reviewed with him the covenant, and reconfirmed it, from several points of view. Recall the Pearl of Great Price, with the Urim and Thummim, and he sees the entire universe, and God tells him that his seed will be as numerous as the stars he sees. He further shows him that the way the universe is set up, it is the same way the Lord has his children set up. Why not. Everything is made to bear record of the Son of God. The universe is the basic pattern of everything he does.

quotes.text: Holy women The Lord never sends apostles and prophets and righteous men to minister to his people without placing women of like spiritual stature at their sides. Adam stands as the great high priest, under Christ, to rule as a natural patriarch over all men of all ages, but he cannot rule alone; Eve, his wife, rules at his side, having like caliber and attainments to his own. Abraham is tested as few men have been when the Lord commands him to offer Isaac upon the altar (Gen. 22:1-19); and Sarah struggles with like problems when the Lord directs that she withhold from the Egyptians her status as Abraham's wife. (Abra. 2:21-25; Gen. 12:7-20.) Isaac gains from the Lord the promise that his seed shall "multiply as the stars of heaven" (Gen. 26:1-4); and Rebekah, his wife, receives a blessing of her own in which she is promised that she shall be "the mother of thousands of millions." (Gen. 24:59-60.) And so it goes, in all dispensations and at all times when there are holy men there are also holy women. Neither stands alone before the Lord. The exaltation of the one is dependent upon that of the other.
quotes.speaker: Bruce R. Mc Conkie
